findings.title: Conditional passkeys are no longer initialized for an unauthenticated login
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` requires a non-null user, but the initial UsernamePasswordForm request has no selected user. Consequently `fillContextForm` is skipped on the initial login page (and again after a bad password clears the user), so the conditional-WebAuthn form/challenge is absent and a user cannot initiate a passkey login from the normal username/password screen. This reverses the prior behavior, which initialized conditional passkeys specifically while no user was selected; the updated integration tests that expect `#webauth` on the initial UsernamePasswordForm page will fail.

findings.title: The test does not actually verify that the WebAuthn form is absent
findings.body: This block catches every `Exception`, including the assertion failure when the form exists and the explicit `fail()` when it does not. As a result, both presence and absence of `#webauth` make the test pass, so the stated regression case (passkeys disabled during re-authentication) is untested. Catch only `NoSuchElementException` or use an explicit absence assertion; the equivalent block at line 313 has the same issue.
